title: Birthdays and Gifts

parts.title: Notices and messages
parts.instructions: For each notice, choose what it means.
notices: PARTY ROOM: Book our party room for your child's birthday. Includes food, a cake and two hours of games. Call to reserve a date.

parts.title: The worst present ever
parts.instructions: Read the article and choose the best answer for each question.
parts.passage:
On my twelfth birthday, my aunt gave me a pair of pink socks. I was not pleased. I had hoped for a bicycle, and I had told everybody in my family about it for months. Instead, I got socks, a card with a cat on it and a hug that lasted too long.

My mother saw my face and whispered, "Say thank you." I did, but I did not smile. Later, I put the socks at the back of a drawer and forgot about them.

A year later, my aunt became ill and spent a long time in hospital. When I visited her, she was in bed, knitting something. She told me that she had made those socks herself, and that she had used the last of her wool. I felt terrible. I went home and found them at once.

I wore them the next day, even though it was summer, and I showed her. She laughed until she cried. Today, I am thirty, and those socks are still in my drawer, although they are too small. I would not give them away for any bicycle in the world.

questions.prompt: What had the writer hoped for?
questions.explanation: She had hoped for a bicycle.
She whispered "Say thank you."

questions.prompt: What did the writer learn about the socks?
questions.explanation: Her aunt had made the socks herself.
She felt terrible.

questions.prompt: What does she think of the socks now?
questions.explanation: She would not give them away for any bicycle.

parts.title: Birthdays around the world
parts.instructions: Choose the sentence that fits each gap. There is one extra sentence.
parts.passage:
People celebrate birthdays in very different ways. [1] In many countries, the main thing is to have a cake with candles, and the birthday child makes a wish before blowing them out.

In some places, there are special customs. [2] For example, in Denmark, the flag is put outside the window on the morning of a birthday.

In Mexico, children often have a piñata. [3] When it breaks, sweets and small toys fall out, and everyone runs to pick them up.

In some parts of China, people eat long noodles on their birthday. [4] They believe that the longer the noodles, the longer the person will live.

Whatever the tradition, the idea is the same. [5] A birthday is a day when family and friends show someone that they are special.
sentences: It is a paper animal filled with treats, and the children hit it with a stick.
The noodles must not be cut, so people try to eat them in one go.
No one has to wait until they are old to enjoy it.
Some of them may surprise visitors.
The way of celebrating may change, but the day is always important.
Cakes are cheaper in supermarkets than in bakeries.

gaps.explanation: Ways of celebrating differ; the next sentence says many countries have a cake.
Some customs may surprise visitors; the next sentence gives Denmark as an example.
The piñata is a paper animal with treats; the next sentence says that when it breaks, sweets fall out.
The noodles must not be cut; the next sentence gives the belief.
Ways of celebrating may change, but the day is always important; the next sentence says the idea is the same.

parts.title: An invitation
parts.instructions: Choose the correct word for each gap.
parts.passage: Dear Ashby, I am having a party [1] my birthday next Saturday, and I would love you to come. It will start at six, [2] you can arrive a little earlier if you want to help me. We are going to have pizza and games [3] the garden. My brother has promised to play music, [4] he usually forgets. Please let me know [5] you can come by Wednesday. Do not bring a present, because I have everything I [6]. See you soon! Talia

questions.explanation: A party for my birthday gives the reason.
But adds a contrast: it starts at six, but you may come earlier.
We use in with the garden: in the garden.
But shows the contrast with he forgets.
Let me know if you can come.
Everything I need: present simple.

parts.title: Choosing a gift
parts.instructions: Write one word in each gap.
parts.passage: Choosing the right gift can be quite difficult. Some people spend weeks thinking [1] what to buy. A good tip is to listen carefully to your friends during the year. They often mention things they would like [2] have. Another idea is to give something you have made yourself. A handmade present shows that you took the trouble [3] think about the person. If you are short of money, [4] not give your time? You could offer to cook a meal or to help with the garden. Remember that it is not the price that matters, [5] the thought behind the gift. And do not forget to wrap it nicely, because a pretty package makes any present seem [6] special.

gaps.explanation: Would like is followed by to and the verb have.
The phrase take the trouble is followed by to and a verb.
Why not followed by a verb is used to make a suggestion.
Not the price but the thought.

parts.title: A message from a party organiser
parts.instructions: Listen to the talk and complete each note with one word.

turns.speaker: organiser
turns.text: Hello, this is Keren from Sunny Parties. I am calling about the birthday party for your daughter on the twenty-second of June. First, the good news: the room is free from two to five. The price is ninety pounds, which includes a clown for an hour. You asked about food. We offer pizza, sandwiches or a hot meal, and most families choose pizza. Remember to tell me how many children are coming by the first of June, because the price depends on that. The maximum is twenty-five. There is a car park behind the building, and it is free on Saturdays. If you want a photographer, we can arrange one for thirty pounds. Please call me back on this number.

gaps.explanation: She says the party is on the twenty-second of June.

gaps.prompt: The room is free from two to ___
gaps.explanation: She says it is free from two to five.
She says the price is ninety pounds.

gaps.prompt: The price includes a ___ for an hour
gaps.explanation: She says it includes a clown for an hour.

gaps.prompt: The maximum number of children is ___
gaps.explanation: She says the maximum is twenty-five.

parts.title: An interview with a cake maker
parts.instructions: Listen to the interview and choose the correct answer.

turns.speaker: i
turns.text: Lyra, you make birthday cakes for a living. How did you start?

turns.speaker: h
turns.text: I made a cake for my brother when I was nine. It fell apart, but he still ate it. I have been baking ever since.

turns.speaker: i
turns.text: What is the strangest cake that you have made?

turns.speaker: h
turns.text: A cake in the shape of a washing machine, for a man who loved cleaning. Inside, it had three layers of chocolate.

turns.speaker: i
turns.text: How long does a big cake take?

turns.speaker: h
turns.text: About two days. I bake on the first day, and I decorate on the second. The decoration is the slow part.

turns.speaker: i
turns.text: What is the hardest thing about your job?

turns.speaker: h
turns.text: Making people happy! They expect the cake to look exactly like the picture in their head, so I always ask lots of questions.

turns.speaker: i
turns.text: Do you eat a lot of cake yourself?

turns.speaker: h
turns.text: Surprisingly, no. After a day of tasting, I prefer a plain piece of toast.

turns.speaker: i
turns.text: What is your advice for people who want to bake at home?

turns.speaker: h
turns.text: Start simple, follow the recipe exactly and never open the oven door too early.

questions.explanation: She says it fell apart, but her brother ate it.

questions.explanation: She says about two days.

questions.prompt: What does she like to eat after a day of tasting?
questions.explanation: She prefers a plain piece of toast.
